38 Two cells of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 3.0 V and 1.2 V and negligible internal resistance are
connected to resistors of resistance 9.0 Ω and 18 Ω as shown.
3.0 V
1.2 V
9.0 Ω
I
18 Ω
What is the current I in the 9.0 Ω resistor?
A
0.10 A
B
0.20 A
C
0.30 A
D
0.47 A

hints: Notice the top branch has the $3.0\text{ V}$ and $1.2\text{ V}$ cells connected positive to positive, so decide whether their e.m.f.s add or subtract.
Notice the top branch, the $9.0\,\Omega$ resistor and the $18\,\Omega$ resistor are all in parallel, so they share the same terminal p.d.
Connect the net e.m.f. to $V = IR$ for the $9.0\,\Omega$ branch using $I = V/9.0$.
walkthrough: Identify the parallel structure from the diagram: the two cells in series form one branch, the $9.0\,\Omega$ resistor is the middle branch, and the $18\,\Omega$ resistor is the bottom branch.
Find the net e.m.f. driving the parallel combination. The cells oppose, so subtract: $V = 3.0 - 1.2 = 1.8\text{ V}$. Internal resistance is negligible, so this is the terminal p.d.
State the parallel rule: all three branches have the same p.d. of $1.8\text{ V}$ across them.
Apply $V = IR$ to the $9.0\,\Omega$ resistor: $I = V/R$.
Substitute with units: $I = 1.8\text{ V} / 9.0\,\Omega = 0.20\text{ A}$, flowing in the direction shown. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $V/R = 1.8/18 = 0.10\text{ A}$, which is the current in the $18\,\Omega$ resistor, not the $9.0\,\Omega$ resistor.

B.explanation: The net p.d. across the parallel branches is $1.8\text{ V}$, so $I = 1.8/9.0 = 0.20\text{ A}$ in the $9.0\,\Omega$ resistor.

C.explanation: This is close to $3.0/9.0 = 0.33\text{ A}$, which incorrectly uses only the $3.0\text{ V}$ cell and ignores the opposing $1.2\text{ V}$ cell.

D.explanation: This is $(3.0+1.2)/9.0 = 0.47\text{ A}$, which incorrectly adds the e.m.f.s when the cells are connected positive to positive and oppose.
